page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 1 vCPU with a dedicated CPU allocation, utilizing an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1 physical core with 1 thread per core, 4.0 GB of system memory providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core, and an L3 cache size of 45 MB. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of this instance in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1088.79, which is categorized in the bottom 25%, while its multi-core score of 1088.79 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show low throughput, with read-only large block uncached transfers at 10.68 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 9.71 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput of 1.21 GB/sec rank in the bottom 10% of tested systems.

Given its entry-level hardware profile, the n1-standard-1 represents a low-resource density option. The primary tradeoff is its limited processing power and memory bandwidth, which restrict its utility for intensive workloads. However, its dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable, albeit low, performance compared to shared-core alternatives. This instance is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, simple text processing, small-scale software compilation, or low-demand development and testing environments that do not require high computational throughput or local storage.
